AcePolicyGate.description:
How the ACE engine treated the call at the moment a policy run completed.

`PolicyEngine.run` emits the SAME `PolicyRunComplete`, with the same
fields, whether (a) the policy chain was EMPTY and the target default
allowed, (b) a policy returned `Allowed`, or (c) every policy returned
`Continue` and the default allowed. So the event proves the target was
attached, `run` was called, and the call was not rejected — it does NOT
prove that any policy evaluated anything. Without this field the three
collapse onto one "a policy run exists" label, and a fail-open gate reads
as screened.

The vocabulary is deliberately the one the router provisioner already uses
for the same question (`workspace_routers::onchain::AceEntryGate`), minus
`Refused`: a refused call reverts and emits no `PolicyRunComplete`, so it
is structurally impossible for a RECORDED run and is not representable
here by construction.

New values may be added; treat unknown values as other.

oneOf.description:
This many policies ran ahead of an allowing default. Always > 0: zero
policies is reported as `open`, which is a different fact.

gate.description: New values may be added; treat unknown values as other.

oneOf.description:
The engine's policy chain for this `(target, selector)` was EMPTY at
the run's block and the run completed, so the default allowed it: the
call passed UNCHECKED. Never counts as coverage.

BondReservation.description: The hub bond reservation backing a bonded RFQ order.

amount.description:
Reserve amount in hub-asset BASE UNITS (decimal string). Convert for

assetSymbol.description:
Hub bond asset symbol (e.g. `USDC`). OMITTED when the order's marker
predates the server-authoritative descriptor — never fabricated: a

decimals.description: Hub bond asset decimals. OMITTED (never defaulted to 0) when unknown.

paidAmount.description:
Hub-asset BASE UNITS the hub ACTUALLY transferred to the taker on a slash
(`SolverSlashed.paid`). `amount` is what was RESERVED and is NOT the same
number when the solver's bond had fallen below its reservations — the hub
pays `min(reserved, bonded)`. Emitted ONLY with `status: slashed`, and only
once the backend has decoded the slash; absent on legacy markers, where a
consumer must stay amount-free rather than quoting `amount`.

Why the order was never bond-eligible. Emitted ONLY with

predates this field sees a byte-identical payload on the paths it knows.

BondUnbondableReason.description:

compensation to (`crossVmCarrier`, `routerCloneBeneficiary`), or the solver's bond
had no free capacity when the order opened (`insufficientFreeBond`).
Present only when the bond status is `notEligible`.

letters, digits, `-` or `_`. Compared exactly, as CAIP-2 references are case-sensitive.

CardFirmness.description:
How firm a card's price is, read with `expiresAt`: `firm: true` delivers exactly
`buy.amount` until `expiresAt`; `firm: false` with `expiresAt` executes held to `minOut`;
`firm: false` with `expiresAt` null is indicative (it lapses at `staleAfter`, and is
orderable only through its `next: order`, executed within the caller's minimum receive).

firm.description: Whether the venue is bound to this price until `expiresAt`.

lastLook.description:
Always false: no venue re-checks an accepted price before it fills, so an order inside
`expiresAt` on a firm card trades at it or is refused unsent.

A Venue's kind: where its money sits. Each Venue declares its kind in the
venue-desk catalogue (`catalogue::Venue.kind`), which re-exports this type.
Published as `CatalogueVenueKind`: the `VenueKind` component is the solver
classifier (`solvers::VenueKind`, solver-operated or direct venue).

Account-linked wallet id that placed the trade, for per-wallet filtering

The catalogue Venue id of the order's LP (`keyrock`, `circle-cctp`; a routed

The typed form of `actionRequired`: the same decision the order page reads
(`OrderResponse.nextAction`), computed by the same backend owner. Clients switch on

Who acts next: the same decision the order read carries.

Canonical route-aware order kind (`cctp-v0` / `composite-v0` / `fx-v0` / …)
for list clients + API-key parity with the detail. Absent for non-route
orders, where `orderType` suffices.

Canonical user-facing order lifecycle status from `orders.status`.

submittedByYou.description:
The caller submitted this order: the same rule as the order read's

`renewal_pending` (a verification renewal is due) and `frozen` (the counterparty
is frozen).

New values may be added; treat unknown values as other.

CreateWebhookResponse.description:
Response after creating a webhook. Store the shown-once `whsec_<base64>` secret now.
Standard Webhooks signs `"<webhook-id>.<webhook-timestamp>.<raw body>"` with the decoded
key bytes, sending `webhook-signature: v1,<base64 HMAC-SHA256>`. No legacy headers are sent.

secret.description: Present only on the first response; receipts and replays contain null.

secretShownOnce.description: True even when the secret has been withheld on replay.

CreditCheck.description: Point-in-time credit evidence, never a reservation or dispatch authority.

positionsBasis.description: Why the read vouches that an omitted asset holds zero; absent when no asset was omitted.

zeroAssets.description: Assets the LP's positions read omitted and that this decision counted as zero.

CreditReservation.description:
A firm ask's combined hold on a credit account: the positives the trade spends
(debit-asset units) and the credit exposure it may add (line currency), admitted together
under the account lock. Held until the quote expires or Confirm adopts it; an indicative
card never carries one. Neither a dispatch authority nor a consent.

expiresAt.description: When the unsent hold is released: the quote's own expiry.

exposureAmount.description: The credit exposure the trade may add, in the line currency, rounded up.

operationId.description: The prepared trade the ask was made for, when it was.

positiveInputAmount.description: The part of the debit spent from positives, in the debit asset, rounded up.

state.description: `reserved` while unsent; `released` once it expired, was adopted or was superseded.

DayBasis.description:
A settlement schedule's day basis.

New values may be added; treat unknown values as other.

DecimalAmount.description:
A non-negative decimal string in Asset units (`"10000"`, `"9994.0"`): digits with an
optional fraction, no sign, exponent or leading zero. Never a float and never base
units. A request amount must also be positive (`INVALID_AMOUNT`); a fee or a
known balance may be zero.

DeferredSettlementInfo.description:
Deferred LP settlement/withdrawal tracking that is separate from the
order's primary execution status. A deferred order can be `Executed` while
this object still reports a settlement window or withdrawal state.

DeliverTo.description:
Output to own money, a third-party payee, or an explicit chain address.

lpSpreadUsd.description:
LP spread charged to the taker (the `lp_spread` fee_kind). Previously this
was miscounted into `user_gas_usd` and displayed as "User Gas"; it is a
pricing spread, not gas.

protocolFeeUsd.description:
The TetraFi platform fee, in USD. `null` when the platform fee has no USD value
recorded (an invoiced fee before it is billed): unpriced is not the same as free.

solverGasUsd.description:
Gas the solver absorbed, in USD. `null` when no priced gas was
recorded for the solver.

totalCostUsd.description: Sum of every priced row; unrecorded gas contributes nothing.

userGasUsd.description:
Gas the taker paid, in USD. `null` when no priced gas was recorded
for the taker: unrecorded is not the same as free.

FeesSection.description: Fee breakdown for a trade: one row per transaction-level fee event (gas on each settlement transaction, protocol fee, solver fee, relayer tip), plus totals by payer (user, solver, protocol).

oneOf.description:

venue account) holds less than the trade debits: send `amount` of `asset` to
`address` on `chain`, then get a new price. `walletId` is the binding target the

oneOf.description:
A bank-funded venue account is short and deposit first isn't offered on it:
its bank side declares no deposit instructions, or nothing that
credits a declared deposit. The account is funded from its own funding details,
then the quote is asked again. `amount` is the shortfall in `currency`;
`connectionId` is the venue account to fund; `reason` is the venue's declared
sentence for why ("Keyrock gives no deposit reference for bank transfers, so
TetraFi can't tell your deposit apart"), product copy without a final period.

LpInfoSection.description:
Section D: LP / counterparty information, including its compliance posture.

For a KYB'd liquidity provider the compliance fields carry the LP's
jurisdiction, KYB status, and regulatory licences — the "who is the other
side and are they authorised" a compliance officer needs. Router/bridge
routes settle through a protocol (CCTP, Relay, …), not a VASP counterparty:
those report `counterparty_type = "protocol"` with no jurisdiction/licences,
which is itself the compliance-relevant fact (no VASP-to-VASP Travel Rule
message is owed).

LpInformationNeeded.description:
One LP whose enforced serving requirement finds a fact the workspace has
not recorded, and the onboarding catalogue items that supply it. Advisory:
it blocks nothing by itself; the trading path refuses with
`LP_REQUIREMENT_INFORMATION_NEEDED` and the same items.

target id or address. A preference, not a choice: a venue account uses it only where it

choice and wins on its chain.

letters, digits, `-` or `_`. Compared exactly, as CAIP-2 references are case-sensitive.

NextAction.description:
What the order needs from its reader next. Absent when nothing is needed.

Each variant is a distinct situation with a distinct remedy; none collapses onto
another, and a state the backend cannot decide yields no action rather than a
`signNextLeg` it cannot back.

New values may be added; treat unknown values as other.

oneOf.description: The payout remains unsent with its venue-account hold retained.

kind.description: New values may be added; treat unknown values as other.

oneOf.description: A bound wallet destination is no longer usable. Funds remain at the LP.

kind.description: New values may be added; treat unknown values as other.

oneOf.description:
The taker signs the next leg. `legIndex` 0 is an FX-first order that has not
started: its funds are still in the taker's wallet.

kind.description: New values may be added; treat unknown values as other.

oneOf.description: The fresh price moved past the tolerance. The taker may accept it once.

kind.description: New values may be added; treat unknown values as other.

oneOf.description:
A leg did not run and the funds came back to the taker: sign it again, on the
same order.

attempt.description: The attempt the retry starts (the ended attempts plus one).

kind.description: New values may be added; treat unknown values as other.

oneOf.description:
The route ended with the funds in the taker's wallet part-way, and no re-quote
owner can resume it: finish the trade from there with a new order.

kind.description: New values may be added; treat unknown values as other.

oneOf.description: The taker stopped waiting, or the wait reached its bound.

kind.description: New values may be added; treat unknown values as other.

oneOf.description: An operator must review the order; the taker cannot act on it.

kind.description: New values may be added; treat unknown values as other.

NextActor.description:
Who must act before the order can progress, shared by the order read and list.

New values may be added; treat unknown values as other.

OAuthErrorResponse.description: An RFC 6749 error response: the token endpoint answers the standard's body, not `ApiError`.

error.description:
The RFC 6749 error code: `invalid_client` (401), `invalid_grant`, `unsupported_grant_type`
or `unauthorized_client` (400), or `temporarily_unavailable` (503).

error_description.description: Why the client was refused, when the RFC 6749 code alone does not say.

error_uri.description:
The error-code reference for a TetraFi cause the RFC 6749 code does not name
(`SIGNED_KEY_NOT_EXCHANGEABLE`).

OAuthTokenRequest.description:
An RFC 6749 client-credentials token request, form-encoded. Its field names are the
standard's, so OAuth client libraries send it unchanged.

client_id.description: The service account's id. Omit it when the credentials are sent with HTTP Basic.

client_secret.description:
The service account's full API key (`tfk_live_…` or `tfk_test_…`). Omit it when the
credentials are sent with HTTP Basic.

access_token.description: The bearer token: send it as `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`.

expires_in.description: Seconds until the token expires (at most 900). Request a new one before then.

OnChainCoverage.description:
On-chain (ACE policy run) coverage for one order.

Evaluated in this order, so a POSITIVE observation always wins over an
explanation: `PolicyRun` → `ProviderLedger` → `NoTxRecorded` →
`LedgerBehind` → `NoPolicyRun`.

New values may be added; treat unknown values as other.

oneOf.description:
At least one recorded ACE policy run matches one of the order's
declared transactions AND that run's gate is `enforced`: a policy
actually evaluated the call.

`runs` carries EVERY joined run, enforced or not, and `open_runs` /
`unknown_runs` count the ones that are not evidence of screening.
Those counts are redundant with `runs` on purpose: an `Open` run is a
fail-open gate that must stay visible even when a sibling run on the
same transaction covered the trade, and a reader that has to fold over
`runs` to notice it is a reader that will not.

state.description: New values may be added; treat unknown values as other.

oneOf.description:
Runs join the order's transactions, NONE is enforced, and at least one
passed unchecked: the engine's policy chain for that
`(target, selector)` was empty and the default allowed it.

Deliberately NOT `policyRun`. `PolicyEngine.run` emits the
same event whether a policy allowed the call or no policy existed at
all, so collapsing this onto "a policy run exists" reports a fail-open
gate as screened.

state.description: New values may be added; treat unknown values as other.

oneOf.description:
Runs join the order's transactions and NONE of their postures could be
established. Neither evidence of screening nor of its absence.

state.description: New values may be added; treat unknown values as other.

oneOf.description:
The order's venue is DECLARED by the contract registry as a deferred
provider-ledger venue (the registry's own OTC path set: `venueType`
`otc` / `cex_spot`, or a solver or venue id the registry classifies
there). Such a venue settles on the provider's books and TetraFi
broadcasts nothing on its behalf, so an absent policy run is correct
by design rather than a gap.

`declaredBy` records the declaration that decided it, so the claim
is auditable.

NOT the same thing as the catalogued scenario's `external_venue`
sub-class, which describes a TetraFi-BROADCAST transaction landing on
registry-declared third-party infrastructure (Circle's
`tokenMessengerV2`, Across's `spokePool`, Circle's `fxEscrow`). The
two are disjoint by construction — this one broadcasts nothing at
all — and they are deliberately not given one shared label.

Limit: the registry declares no property that separates a venue whose
execution reaches a TetraFi contract (e.g. `octarine-rwa`, an `onchain`
direct venue that executes through a TetraFi swap contract) from one
whose execution does not (e.g. a `circle-cctp` taker burn straight to
Circle's TokenMessengerV2). Those are reported as `noPolicyRun`.

state.description: New values may be added; treat unknown values as other.

oneOf.description:
The order declares no transaction hash in any of its own or its
settlement's fields, so there is nothing to match.

state.description: New values may be added; treat unknown values as other.

oneOf.description:
The order declares transactions, no event joins them, and the ACE
event ledger is not current for at least one of the order's
candidate chains — so the absence is inconclusive.

state.description: New values may be added; treat unknown values as other.

oneOf.description:
The order declares transactions, the ledger is current for every
candidate chain, and no policy-run event exists. Provisional: the
catalogued scenario's RPC probe sub-classifies each one.

state.description: New values may be added; treat unknown values as other.

OnChainSettlementSection.description:
Section B: On-chain settlement data.

Models the four-step lifecycle of an intent on-chain: `submit_tx` (user
deposit / intent creation), `fill_tx` (solver fill on destination chain),
`proof_tx` (cross-chain proof submission), `finalise_tx` (claim/settle on
origin). Oracle + settlement_stage describe the proof-relay layer.

oneOf.description: Confirmed CEX ledger stages, including venue evidence and the DDR v2 forward.

failureReason.description: A human-readable failure reason when status is `failed` or `refunded`.

transactions.description:
Generic per-stage transaction list — the full timeline for ANY order kind
(escrow quartet, bridge/relay/FX legs, composite hops), each row enriched with
a `label`, an `explorerUrl`, and a `legIndex`. The escrow-shaped
`submit/fill/proof/finalise` refs above stay for back-compat; this list is what
non-escrow (router/composite/FX) orders render, and it is empty (not a wall of
"—") when an order has no recorded transactions.

OrderChannel.description: New values may be added; treat unknown values as other.

OrderComplianceCheck.description: One compliance check that ran for the order.

chainId.description: Chain the check was evaluated against, when on-chain.

contractAddress.description: Contract the check was evaluated against (policy engine, escrow).

details.description: One-line human summary recorded by the check.

enforced.description:
Whether the recorded mode enforced this check; false for unrecorded modes is
not a claim that the historical gate admitted its failures.

evidence.description: Structured evidence recorded by the check, secret-scrubbed.

groupReason.description: An explanation based only on this row's recorded applicability and outcome.

missingInput.description: The input that was missing: verified_notional_usd, eur_usd_reference_rate or workspace_compliance_policy.

reasonCode.description: Why a check could not be concluded: NOTIONAL_UNVERIFIED, REFERENCE_RATE_UNAVAILABLE or COMPLIANCE_POLICY_UNAVAILABLE, from its recorded evidence.

runModeReason.description: Present only when a stored mode cannot be decoded; never a default mode.

source.description: Provider or engine that produced the verdict (`pretrade_checks.data_source`).

txHash.description: Transaction that commits the evidence, when one exists.

OrderComplianceDenialFact.description: Typed denial metadata; withheld reasons require generic compliance-review copy.

OrderComplianceScope.description:
Whether the caller may read the recorded compliance details for this order.

New values may be added; treat unknown values as other.

OrderComplianceSection.description:
The order's own compliance verdict and every check that ran for it, split into
on-chain and off-chain checks.

checks.description: Every check that ran, oldest first. Denying check first when denied.

corridor.description: `"<origin chain id>-><destination chain id>"` when both are known.

denialReason.description: Why the order was denied, when it was.

evaluatedAt.description: When the gate evaluated the order (earliest recorded check).

oneOf.description:
Whether an on-chain ACE policy run covers this order's transactions; it
always agrees with the workspace order-coverage audit.

`null` and `noTxRecorded` are DIFFERENT facts: `null` means coverage could
not be determined for this response, while `noTxRecorded` means the order
declares no transaction at all. Never read `null` as a finding about the order.

OrderExecutionReport.description: Flattened into both order kinds' envelopes: its keys are the envelope's own keys.

fees.description:
The fees actually charged, as recorded: the venue's own fee report, bridge fees, network
gas the order's wallet paid, and the platform fee. Never a quoted estimate. A fee whose
amount was not reported or could not be read is left out rather than shown as 0, and its
kind is listed in `unrecordedFees`.

fills.description:
Each confirmed fill, in execution order. Always present: empty before any fill is
confirmed.

quotedBuyAmount.description:
The buy amount the executed quote said would land. Null when it is not known (for
example before a venue order is dispatched).

settledBuyAmount.description:
What actually landed, read from the fill or settlement evidence. Null until it is
measured; never the quote carried forward and never 0 for unknown.

settlesBy.description:
The latest time the order settles, or can no longer execute, under its recorded terms:
the signed order's fill deadline, or, on a route, the latest fill deadline every leg
commits to (Advanced); the last on-chain step's send-by time (an on-chain Basic swap).
Null when no such term is recorded, for example a same-chain DEX swap, whose call
carries no deadline.

unrecordedFees.description:
Every fee kind the order incurs whose actual charge is not recorded or could not be
read: a venue fee taken inside the price without an amount, a bridge leg's fee, gas
the order's wallet spent without a readable receipt, a platform fee billed off the
order. Always present; empty only when every incurred charge is in `fees`. An absent
kind with no `fees` line means nothing of that kind was charged. Open set: clients
show an unknown kind generically.

OrderFailure.description: Structured order failure details for programmatic polling clients.

code.description: Stable coarse code for client branching.

message.description: The code's fixed, user-safe sentence. Never the executor's own error text.

phase.description: Lifecycle phase where the failure was observed.

recoveryStopped.description:
True when recovery has written this order off as permanently unrecoverable: it will
not be retried. False while recovery may still resume it.

OrderFailurePhase.description:
Transaction phase of a public order failure.

New values may be added; treat unknown values as other.

chain.description: The CAIP-2 chain the fee was paid on, for an on-chain charge.

includedInPrice.description:
True when the venue took this fee inside its price: the fill amounts already reflect
it, so it is not charged on top of them.

OrderFeeKind.description:
What a fee paid for.

New values may be added; treat unknown values as other.

OrderFill.description: One confirmed fill: what it delivered, what it spent and where.

amount.description:
The buy Asset amount this fill delivered. Null when the fill is confirmed but nothing
measured its delivery.

at.description:
The recorded fill time: the venue's fill time or the time the fill transaction was
observed. Null when no fill time was recorded.

network.description: The CAIP-2 chain of `txHash`; absent off-chain.

oneOf.description:
The executed price in market convention (quote units per one base unit). Null when
either amount is unknown.

sellAmount.description: The sell Asset amount this fill spent. Null when it was not recorded.

txHash.description: The fill's or settlement's on-chain transaction; absent off-chain.

OrderFillPrice.description: An executed price: `amount` units of `quote` for one unit of `base`.

OrderFillVenue.description: The venue that executed the fill, by the same id and name its quote carried.

OrderGrantRefusal.description: New values may be added; treat unknown values as other.

OrderLegExternalRef.description: An off-chain provider reference for a leg.

kind.description: Reference kind, e.g. `circleTradeId` | `acrossDepositId` | `relayRequestId`.

url.description: A provider status URL for `value`, when one is known.

buy.description:
What the leg quote ESTIMATED this leg would buy. Always the quote: a confirmed
delivery is reported separately in `measuredBuy` rather than overwriting this,
so the two facts stay distinguishable on the wire.

oneOf.description:
Per-leg counterparty compliance posture — WHO filled this leg and their
regulatory standing. Absent on the generic `OrderResponse`; populated only
on the admin company trade-detail. Lets a composite show "leg 1 = KYB'd
Solver X (Cayman Islands), leg 2 = CCTP protocol" instead of one collapsed
counterparty.

etaSeconds.description:
The route quote's per-leg ETA in seconds, when it carried one: the venue's
estimate of this leg's own execution. For a CCTP leg it is the burn-to-mint
upper bound of the chosen finality tier, set by the source chain (Fast ~20 s;
Standard ~19 min from the L1-anchored chains). It never counts the time a
parked route waits for its taker to sign the next leg.

externalRefs.description:
Off-chain provider references for the leg (Circle trade id, Across deposit id,
Relay request id, …) — the identifiers a client uses to look the leg up on the
provider's own status surface.

feeUsd.description:
Concrete USD-denominated fee total for this leg. Absent when the route
quote only carried spread/fee bps or a non-USD fee asset.

index.description: 0-indexed position in the route's execution order.

kind.description:
Normalised leg mechanism: `cctp` | `across` | `relay` | `fx` | `solver`, or the
raw `providerProduct` for a kind the backend does not special-case (clients must
treat this as an open set and fall back to a generic presentation).

label.description: Human-friendly leg label, e.g. `"Circle CCTP Fast"` or `"CCTP: Base → Arc"`.

oneOf.description:
What this leg was OBSERVED to deliver, from the settlement receipt TetraFi
recorded for this leg, in the leg's buy asset. Absent until that receipt has
confirmed the leg, which a client must render as "not measured": never as
zero, and never by silently showing `buy` in its place.

This is the only place an INTERMEDIATE leg's real delivery appears. On a
`StableFX -> CCTP` composite the FX leg settles a different asset on a
different chain from the order's own output, so the order-level delivery
cannot describe it.

measuredBuySource.description:
Which settlement receipt backed `measuredBuy`: `circleSettledOutput`
| `cctpVerifiedOutput` | `relayVerifiedOutput` | `solverVerifiedOutput`
| `nativeUniswapOutcome`. Carried so an operator can trace a per-leg number back
to the observation that produced it instead of inferring it from the leg kind.

product.description:
The venue product of a firm-RFQ leg: `lop` (Octarine limit order) | `rfq` (Bebop
PMM RFQ) | `bopamm` (Bebop BopAMM). Read from the handoff persisted for the leg,
so it is absent until the venue firmed it and on every non-RFQ leg. An open set:
a client renders an unknown value generically.

provider.description: Venue / provider display name for the leg.

sell.description:
What the leg sells: its asset, chain and `decimalAmount`, or `unresolved` when
the backend cannot scale it.

status.description: Leg status: `pending` | `executing` | `done` | `failed` | `refunded`.

oneOf.description:
The money-movement facts of a hosted venue trade's leg: a
payout or pay-in over a bank rail or a chain. Absent on route legs.

transactions.description:
The transactions this leg produced (a subset of the order's `transactions[]`,
correlated by `leg_index`/chain), each already enriched with an explorer URL.

venueRouteId.description:
The venue route identity that filled this leg, from the retained route quote's
`legQuotes[].solverId`. A solver-LP leg carries a real solver id that
resolves to a KYB'd LP workspace; a bridge leg carries a synthetic id
(e.g. `"circle-cctp"`) with no LP workspace behind it. This is the handle
the trade-detail builder uses to resolve per-leg counterparty compliance.

OrderListKind.description: Which native owner holds an order.

OrderListResponse.description:
A page of the workspace's orders, newest first. A status filter keeps reading until the page
has `limit` items or the orders end, within a bounded scan: a page shorter than `limit` with a
`nextCursor` means that scan reached its limit (`scanLimitReached`), never that the orders ended.

scanLimitReached.description:
True when a status-filtered page stopped at its scan limit before filling `limit`:
more orders remain to examine, so follow `nextCursor`. False on every other page.

OrderRecordsScope.description:
Access to the order's workspace trade records, using the detail/timeline rule.

New values may be added; treat unknown values as other.

oneOf.description: The hub bond reservation backing a bonded RFQ order: its lifecycle status and reserve amount. Absent for non-bonded orders.

The order's own compliance verdict and every check that ran, split
on-chain / off-chain. Readable by whoever may read the order; workspace
BI stays on the trade-detail endpoint. Absent when the compliance
verdict could not be read for this response.

How each leg after the first runs and where its funds wait if it cannot. Absent
for single-leg orders.

custodySigningError.description:
Why custody signing failed, readable by the user and operators, when
`custodySigningStatus` is `failed` / `failed_unreachable`; absent otherwise.

custodySigningStatus.description:
Custody-signing status for orders a custody provider signs (Fireblocks / BitGo /
DFNS / Copper): `pending` (submitted to the provider, awaiting its signature),
`signed`, `failed`, or `failed_unreachable` (the provider neither called back nor
answered a status check in time). Absent for orders that are not custody-signed.

custodyVaultAddress.description: Custody vault that signed a backend-signed order (`orders.custody_vault_address`).

oneOf.description:
What the settlement evidence says was ACTUALLY delivered, in the order's
buy asset: its symbol, decimals, chain and `decimalAmount`, or `unresolved`.
`route.buy` is what the quote promised; this is the delivery. Absent when
nothing has been captured yet (the order has not settled). Never guessed
from the quote: read `deliveredBuyProvenance` before rendering it.

deliveredBuyProvenance.description:
Where `deliveredBuy` came from: `"measured"` when it was read
back from settlement evidence (a receipt-backed bridge delivery, a
realized DEX output, a Circle-settled FX output, a deferred settlement's
executed amount), `"quoted"` when a quote-time value was carried forward
because nothing measured the delivery.

This field is the whole point of the pair. The lifecycle falls back to
the quoted output when no measurement exists, which makes "measured,
zero slippage" and "never measured" byte-identical — `realizedSlippageBps`
reads 0 for both and `deliveredBuy` repeats the quote. A client
that renders a delivered amount without reading this is reporting a
quote as a receipt.

directUserId.description: Broker-onboarded direct user this order was submitted for.

executionDeadlineAt.description:
Deadline by which execution had to complete before the TTL watchdog
marks the order expired (`orders.execution_deadline_at`).

executionDeadlineKind.description:
Why `executionDeadlineAt` exists: `enforced` (configured SLA) or the
product default (`orders.execution_deadline_kind`).

oneOf.description: Structured failure details when status is failed.

feeOutputs.description:
The order's further signed outputs after `route.buy`, in order: the platform
fee paid to its collector on an order that carries one. Each names its asset,
chain and `decimalAmount`, or `unresolved`. Empty when the order has a single
output.

feeUsd.description: Total fee paid by the user in USD (`orders.fee_usd`).

filledAt.description: When the fill transaction was observed (`orders.filled_at`).

legAttempts.description:
Ended attempts per leg of a multi-leg route, keyed by leg index. The attempt in
progress is the number of ended attempts plus one. Absent until a leg has ended
an attempt.

legs.description:
Uniform per-leg execution model for multi-leg route orders: one entry per
step of the route, in execution order. Absent for single-leg escrow / deferred orders, whose
`transactions[]` timeline is the whole story. Leg status is projected from
the route cursor and can temporarily trail a mined transaction; correlate
it with `transactions[]` and provider references before treating `pending`
as evidence that execution did not occur.

oneOf.description: The same server-owned lifecycle status the trade list carries.

linkedWalletId.description: Linked wallet used for settlement. Absent for older orders.

oneOf.description:
What this multi-leg order needs from its reader next: sign the next leg, accept a
moved price, retry a leg that did not run, finish the trade, or nothing because it
stopped or is under review. Absent when nothing is needed. Computed by the backend
from the route's durable state; clients switch on `kind` and never infer it from
`substatus`, which keeps its own meaning.

nextActions.description:
Follow-up signed actions the client must perform after submit (e.g. the
Circle StableFX Permit2 funding signature). Empty for single-step orders.
Terminal orders and consumed or expired composite permits expose no action.
Clients must still submit the exact permit and retain it for idempotent retries.

oneOf.description: Who must act next, including follow-up signatures visible only on the order read.

orderKind.description:
Canonical, route-aware order kind for status/history + SDK clients
(`cctp-v0` / `across-v4` / `relay-v0` / `fx-v0` / `composite-v0` / `escrow-v0` /
`deferred` / …). Always present. Prefer this over `order_type`, which collapses
routes to `generic-v0`.

pairQuoteId.description:
The held pair-quote id (`q_…`) the order was placed by (`POST /orders {quoteId}`):
the id Review and the quote card showed. `quoteId` above is the executable quote the
order ran on, which can differ. Recorded server-side from the held quote, never from the
request; absent for orders placed with a full quote body and for orders placed before
it was recorded.

realizedSlippageBps.description:
Realized adverse slippage in basis points, computed at settlement as
`10000 * (quoted_output - delivered_output) / quoted_output`. Negative
means the delivery beat the quote.

Deliberately NOT named `slippageBps`: this response already carries
`slippageToleranceBps`, which is the tolerance the order was SUBMITTED
with — a quote-time input, not an outcome. Two fields one word apart
that mean "what I allowed" and "what I got" is how a caller ends up
charting the limit as the result, so the outcome names itself.

Only meaningful alongside `deliveredBuyProvenance == "measured"`; a
`"quoted"` provenance makes this structurally 0.

recipientAddress.description:
Wallet that receives the output: the fill's recipient when known, else
the signed intent / route preview receiver. A workspace-router proxy is
reported as-is; it forwards to the taker at settlement.

oneOf.description: Optional reporting guidance; never changes order execution status.

route.description:
What the order sells (`route.sell`) and buys (`route.buy`): the asset's
symbol, name, decimals and chain, the base-unit amount and the amount
scaled by those decimals (`decimalAmount`). These are the amounts the
accepted quote committed; `deliveredBuy` reports delivery.

When TetraFi cannot resolve a side, `decimalAmount` is absent and
`unresolved` names why (`assetNotInRegistry`, `amountUnavailable`), so a
client renders an explicit unresolved state and never scales base units
itself.

senderAddress.description:
Wallet that funds the order: the signed intent's depositor (escrow /
eip3009 message `sponsor` / `user` / `signer` / `from`), the route
preview's input owner, or the StableFX taker. Absent when the order
recorded none.

settlementSpeedMs.description: `settled_at - created_at` in milliseconds, captured at settlement.

slippageToleranceBps.description:
Client-selected slippage tolerance in basis points: the deferred/OTC submit
tolerance, or for a multi-leg route the tolerance each continuation re-quote may
absorb (the quote request's `intent.metadata.allowedSlippageBps`, default 30).

status.description:
Coarse current status of the order. Terminality is order-kind dependent:
route and atomic venue orders normally complete at `settled`, while
claim-based or deferred products may continue to `finalized`. Use
`substatus` for the route/provider state and do not wait for `finalized`
unconditionally.

stuckSince.description: Last update of a nonterminal order that is stuck waiting on its counterparty.

substatus.description:
Finer-grained state within `status`, when one applies. Route orders surface the
`routeStatus` (`bridging` / `arrived` / `manualReview` / …); escrow/deferred
orders surface the fine wire states the coarse `status` hides (`postFilled` / …).

substatusCode.description:
Machine-readable reason for the current `substatus`, when the client needs
to choose a recovery action without parsing `substatusMessage`.

substatusMessage.description: Human-readable elaboration of `substatus` (e.g. a Circle StableFX status line).

terminal.description:
Whether the order lifecycle is terminal and cannot advance any further.
This is computed by the backend from the product-specific state machine;
clients should poll this field instead of inferring terminality from the
coarse `status` or `substatus` vocabulary.

oneOf.description: Descriptive stage estimates and server-observed clocks. Never an execution deadline.

transactions.description:
Best-effort transaction references for observed lifecycle stages, enriched at
serve time with `label` + `explorerUrl` + `legIndex`. Projection can lag the
chain/provider; absence is not proof that no transaction was submitted.

updatedAt.description: When the response was last updated

venueRouteId.description:
The venue route identity that fills the order, not the catalogue Venue id.
Runtime solver identities and router/composite sentinels are retained verbatim.

oneOf.description: Caller-relative ownership and records visibility, absent when membership is unknown.

workspaceId.description:
Workspace that placed this order. Absent for older orders and for orders placed
with an API key.

elapsedSeconds.description: Automated elapsed time at OrderTiming.observedAt; absent for incomplete history.

key.description: Semantic identity, independent of translated labels and rail positions.

OrderStatus.description:
Coarse public lifecycle status. Failure detail belongs only to `failure`.

New values may be added; treat unknown values as other.

OrderTransactionActor.description:
Actor that submitted a lifecycle transaction.

New values may be added; treat unknown values as other.

OrderTransactionChainRole.description:
Chain role for a lifecycle transaction.

New values may be added; treat unknown values as other.

OrderTransactionInfo.description:
A transaction in an order's timeline, for one lifecycle stage.

`legIndex`, `label` and `explorerUrl` are optional: they tell a client which route
leg the transaction belongs to, a human role label, and a ready-to-open explorer URL.

explorerUrl.description:
Block-explorer URL for `hash` on `chainId` when TetraFi knows the chain's explorer;
when absent, the client falls back to its own per-chain explorer list.

label.description:
Human-friendly role label (e.g. "Bridge burn", "Fill", "Claim"); when absent
the client derives it from `stage`.

legIndex.description: 0-indexed route leg this tx belongs to (multi-leg routes only).

timestamp.description:
Unix seconds at which the platform OBSERVED this transaction: when TetraFi
recorded it, never the block time.

Absent when TetraFi does not know when the transaction happened. A client
must render "time unknown" then, never substitute a time of its own (such as
the order's `updatedAt`).

OrderTransactionStage.description:
Order lifecycle stage that a transaction belongs to.

New values may be added; treat unknown values as other.

OrderTransactionStatus.description:
Transaction status for an order lifecycle stage.

New values may be added; treat unknown values as other.

OrderTravelRuleStatus.description: Travel-rule status snapshot for the order.

required.description:
When applicability is undetermined, `false` is not a claim that the
rule is unnecessary; clients must read `status`.

status.description: `not_required` | `required` | `transmitted` | `not_recorded`.

OrderTxRef.description:
A transaction an order declares, plus WHICH field declared it.

`source` is load-bearing: a hash reached through
`settlement.data.route.legs[1].transactionHash` is a different leg of the
order from `orders.submit_tx_hash`, and a coverage gap on one says
nothing about the other.

chainId.description:
Chain declared alongside the hash, when the declaring object also
declares one. Absent means the settlement did not say — NOT "chain
zero" and not "same chain as the order".

source.description:
Dotted path of the field that declared this hash, e.g.
`orders.submit_tx_hash` or `settlement.data.directDexExecution.transactionHash`.

OrderViewer.description: Caller-relative context for an authenticated read of a workspace-tagged order.

submittedByYou.description: The caller owns the linked wallet or is the order's recorded submitting user.

OrderWalletIdentity.description: The wallet-identity binding proven at admission.

chainFamily.description: `evm` | `solana` | `tron` | … as the linked-wallet registry records it.

OwnBankVerificationMatchedBy.description: New values may be added; treat unknown values as other.

OwnBankVerificationSource.description: New values may be added; treat unknown values as other.

OwnBankVerificationState.description: New values may be added; treat unknown values as other.

amount.description: Exact decimal text, never a floating-point approximation.

OwnedSolverIdentity.description:
Minimal owned identity for historical LP reads. No connection configuration,
credentials, routing grants or counterparty identities are disclosed.

allOf.description: The card's firmness, written as `firm` and `lastLook`.

advisories.description: Competing mechanisms' limitations remain visible even when one serves.

oneOf.description: The bond backing the quote, separate from its firmness; null when unbonded.

basis.description: Where the price came from: a live venue quote, published levels, or a model.

buy.description:
What the taker buys: `buy.amount` is what lands at `deliverTo`, after every
`included: true` fee taken in the bought Asset.

corridors.description: The venue's other supported corridors; changing one is a Requote.

oneOf.description: Expected time to delivery (ISO 8601 duration); null when the venue states none.

expiresAt.description: When an executable quote stops being orderable; null for an indicative one (see `staleAfter`).

oneOf.description: What happens to the input if execution fails, as the venue reports it.

fees.description:
Every fee line, its payer and whether `buy.amount` already includes it; an amount that could
not be read is null, never 0.

oneOf.description:
When this card's venue gives its binding price, from the venue's own declaration:
`onRequest` (a desk is firm-asked by Get firm quote or a requote) or `atExecution`
(the venue prices firm only when the order executes, so Get firm quote is not offered).
Absent when no venue declares it (protocol routes, order books, fiat venues).

firmAskAvailableAt.description:
When this desk takes its next firm ask: its firm-quote limit for this workspace is reached
until then, so Get firm quote and an order-time ask are refused before it. Absent
when no limit is known here; the desk's admission still decides at ask time.

oneOf.description: Current workspace/venue firm asks, read without contacting the provider.

id.description:
The held quote's id (`q_` + ULID): order it with `POST /orders {quoteId}`, preflight it with
`POST /orders/preflight {quoteId}`, requote it with `POST /quotes {requote: id}`. It belongs to the
principal that asked; another principal reads it as unknown (404).

legs.description:
One leg per venue the quote runs through, in execution order: a multi-leg route (for example
CCTP then Circle StableFX) lists each leg's venue and location.

location.description: Where the quote executes, derived from its legs.

oneOf.description:
The most `sell.amount` a `receiveExact` venue card may debit: the mirror of `minOut`, the quoted
debit grown by `priceProtectionBps`. It is the consent an order on it carries, so Confirm's
one fresh quote of an expired card is judged by it. Absent for `payExact`.
The native mechanism that actually supplied this venue's price.
The least `buy.amount` execution may deliver (from `priceProtectionBps`).

minReceiveRequired.description:
Whether `POST /orders` requires `minReceive` for this card. A held firm offer
already supplies confirmation; other within-limit cards need the caller's minimum.

netReceived.description:
`buy.amount` minus every other cost, converted at the Reference mid: for
comparison and sort only, never what lands.

next.description:
The caller's next call: `preflight` (protocol), `order`, `requote` (a production venue's indicative
card: its firm quote comes from a requote), or what to fix first.

observedAt.description:
When the price was observed: an indicative price, or the book read an executable
order-book estimate (one that reprices when chosen) was priced from; null for a firm quote.

readiness.description: Whether the quote can be ordered now (funding, gas, wallet); an unknown is `unavailable`, never 0.

refundClaimableAfter.description:
With `refundOnSource` on an escrowed intent: the instant after which the source-chain
escrow refunds the input if the order was not filled, read from the signed order's own
expiry (`expires`). Until then the input stays in that escrow. Absent when the quote holds
no escrowed intent or its expiry could not be read; never estimated.

requoteOf.description:
The quote this one requoted (`POST /quotes {requote}`); the original stays orderable until its own
expiry, and a route's requote is that same route.

retainUntil.description:
The last instant this held quote can still be requoted, or ordered where its lapse
allows it: its lapse plus the requote window (10 minutes), or the recovery window
(30 minutes) for a protocol quote. After it, requote and order answer 410
`REQUOTE_WINDOW_CLOSED` with `next: search` (request quotes again); before it, an
order past the quote's lapse answers 410 `QUOTE_EXPIRED` with `next: requote`. Read from the held quote's own retention, never computed by a client;
absent when that instant is not representable.

oneOf.description: The bound wallet's screening state; null when no wallet is bound.

sell.description: What the taker sells: Asset, chain (null off-chain), variant and amount in Asset units.

signaturesRequired.description:
Every signature the order needs. `next.sign` carries the first; later ones arrive
on the order as `signNextLeg`.

oneOf.description: Provider bounds retained with this answer, never a current admission grant.

spreadFromMidBps.description: The price's distance from the Reference mid, or the reason it is unknown.

staleAfter.description: When an indicative price goes stale; null for an executable quote.

oneOf.description:
What a `payExact` card leaves unspent of the amount asked: an order book fills whole
lots, so the card spends less and the rest stays where it is paid from. Absent when the card
spends the whole amount.

walletSelection.description: Why each Basic on-chain wallet was selected. Response metadata, never request authority.

propertyNames.description:
A CAIP-2 chain id (`eip155:8453`, `solana:<genesis>`, `tron:shasta`), syntax-checked:
a namespace of 3 to 8 lowercase letters, digits or `-`, and a reference of 1 to 32
letters, digits, `-` or `_`. Compared exactly, as CAIP-2 references are case-sensitive.

PairQuote.description:
One venue's quote for the pair. Every field is always present; one that does not
apply to the quote's firmness is `null`:

| field | indicative | executable, firm | executable, non-firm |
|---|---|---|---|
| `firm` | false | true | false |
| `expiresAt` | null | set | set |
| `minOut` | null | null | set |
| `observedAt`, `staleAfter` | set | null | null |

A stub (`sources[].priceOnRequest`) is indicative with `null` amounts.

The example is an executable non-firm quote: 10000 USDC paid,
`buy.amount` 9996.0 USDT lands after the included 4.0 USDT provider fee;
`netReceived` 9994.8 also subtracts the 0.0004 ETH network fee the taker pays
separately (`included: false`, about 1.2 USDT at the Reference mid), so it is lower
than `buy.amount`; `minOut` 9966.01 (30 bps) bounds `buy.amount`, not
`netReceived`.

PairQuoteFilters.description: Narrowing filters; an omitted filter means all.

PairQuoteRequest.description:
The public fresh `POST /quotes` body: what the taker sells and buys, and exactly one of
`sellAmount` (an exact-in quote) or `buyAmount` (an exact-out quote). Everything else
refines it.

buy.description: The Asset the taker buys, and optionally its chain.

oneOf.description:
The exact amount to buy, a positive decimal string in Asset units. Exactly one of
`sellAmount` and `buyAmount`.

onBehalfOf.description: The direct user a broker quotes for.

preferredWallets.description:
Per CAIP-2 chain: a wallet the caller prefers to sell from, by target id or address. A
preference, not a choice: a venue account uses it only where it is one of that account's
linked wallets on the venue's network, and otherwise quotes from its own default; a venue is
never refused because of it. `source.tradingWallets` is the explicit choice and wins on its chain.

propertyNames.description:
A CAIP-2 chain id (`eip155:8453`, `solana:<genesis>`, `tron:shasta`), syntax-checked:
a namespace of 3 to 8 lowercase letters, digits or `-`, and a reference of 1 to 32
letters, digits, `-` or `_`. Compared exactly, as CAIP-2 references are case-sensitive.

priceProtectionBps.description: The bound between a non-firm executable quote and what execution delivers.

sell.description: The Asset the taker sells, and optionally its chain.

oneOf.description:
The exact amount to sell, a positive decimal string in Asset units. Exactly one of
`sellAmount` and `buyAmount` (400 `INVALID_REQUEST` naming both otherwise).
Default `netReceived`.

Collection deadline, an ISO 8601 duration; default `PT6S`, at least 100 milliseconds and at
most `PT10S`.

PairQuoteSet.description: The JSON reply, and the SSE `complete` event.

quoteRequestId.description:
The quote set's id (`rq_…`), read back at `GET /quotes/requests/{quoteRequestId}`.
The HTTP request id is separate (`X-Request-Id`, an error body's `requestId`).

oneOf.description:
The Reference mid this request's cards were priced against, read once per request.
Absent when the read failed or ran past its budget: the cards then read
`noReferenceMid`, never a spread of 0.

sourceOptions.description:
The trading wallets this caller may name in `source.tradingWallets`, per network:
each one's stored financial account (`acct_…`), scoped to the principal (an API key
sees only the organisation wallets granted to it). Sent even when no card was priced,
so an unbound request learns what to bind. Empty when none is usable.

sources.description: Every considered venue, with its outcome.

venueAsked.description:
Whether answering this request contacted any venue (a live or firm ask), always
sent; `false` when every quote came from cache.

PayBalance.description:
One chain's read of the sell Asset in the caller's Default-binding wallet.

PolicyRunRef.description: One on-chain ACE policy run observed for an order's transaction.

blockNumber.description: The block this run landed in, when known.

enforced.description:
Whether the engine ENFORCED the policy (vs observe-only). Distinct
from `gate`: this says whether the observation BLOCKED
admission, that says whether any policy ran at all.

gate.description:

number of policies that ran), `open` (no policy, the default allowed it)

so EVM and non-EVM transactions each carry their own fields.

PreflightMessageEncoding.description:
Encoding of the exact bytes presented to a non-EVM wallet.

New values may be added; treat unknown values as other.

details.description:
Protocol wallet actions expose `effectiveFloor` as a decimal string in the
output asset's base units: the signed execution's minimum output. Preflight
refuses signing guidance when that bound cannot be read.

oneOf.description:
Exact byte message a non-EVM wallet must authorize. This is separate
from `typedData` so clients never coerce an Ed25519 source permit into
EIP-712 or sign an opaque value extracted from `details`.

Owner-factor preparation for the explicitly selected signing wallet.
This does not authorize signing or imply a reusable delegation grant.

PreflightSourceAuthorizationMessageV1.description:
Exact source-permit message a wallet signs before an API relayer submits
the corresponding source transaction.

message.description: Canonical base64 bytes returned by the versioned protocol builder.

nonce.description:
Canonical unsigned u64 decimal string. JSON numbers cannot preserve the
full replay-nonce domain in JavaScript clients.

signer.description: Case-sensitive base58 wallet expected to sign the message.

PreflightSourceAuthorizationScheme.description:
Scheme carried by a typed non-EVM source-authorization action.

New values may be added; treat unknown values as other.

allOf.description:
Written as `firm` and `lastLook`, both always false: a price binds no venue. Uses the
card's one firmness writer, so a row and a card never disagree on the shape.

oneOf.description: `levels` or `model`; `null` when the row holds no price.
`incremental` whenever `levels` is present.

levels.description: The venue's own levels, normalized to incremental, in sell units.

oneOf.description:
Where the price executes; `null` on a row with no cached corridor (a venue that
holds nothing for the pair).

sizes.description: One entry per requested size, in request order; empty when the row holds no price.

spreadFromMidBps.description:
At the first size, against the Reference mid; `unavailable` when the mid cannot be
read, never 0.

PriceRow.description: One venue's price for one location and variant pair.

PriceRowStatus.description:
A row's outcome:

| status | meaning |
|---|---|
| `priced` | a fresh cached price |
| `stale` | past `staleAfter`, or a private source still warming; any price kept |
| `unsupported` | `pairNotServed`: the venue holds nothing for the pair; `priceSourceNone`: it publishes no price (asked only on `POST /quotes`); `buyAmountUnsupported` |
| `belowMin` | the first size is under the source's minimum |
| `insufficientDepth` | the source cannot fill the first size |
| `needsWallet` | the venue prices only for a wallet |
| `restricted` | a gate keeps the desk price from this principal |
| `unavailable` | a read failed, or a fee could not be computed; `notYetPublished`: the venue publishes this pair and nothing is cached for it yet |

New values may be added; treat unknown values as other.

QuoteSourceEntry.description:
One considered venue's outcome, a closed set tagged `status`:

| status | meaning |
|---|---|
| `asking` | in flight on the stream only: the auction is consulting this venue now; its final outcome replaces it under the same venue key, and none remains at `complete` |
| `answered` | the venue produced a quote |
| `needsWallet` | no wallet of `family` to ask with |
| `walletRefused` | the bound wallet is refused (`Revoked`, a confirmed sanctions hit) |
| `firmQuoteLimited` | a desk's firm-quote cap applies; `explanation` is product copy |
| `priceOnRequest` | no venue price was requested; `quoteId` identifies the held estimate or stub to Requote |
| `askLimitReached` | the venue's ask limit is reached for now; `retryAfter` says when to ask again |
| `timedOut` | no answer inside the deadline |
| `refused` | the venue refused the live ask |
| `restricted` | a gate kept the venue from this principal |
| `unsupported` | the venue does not serve the pair |
| `filteredOut` | the request's own filters exclude it (never a coverage or chain gap) |
| `unavailable` | a read failed (`admissionUnavailable`, …) |

An unscreened default wallet is not a status: the quote carries `screening`. `venue`
is the venue block, its `id` the one quote legs and `/prices` rows carry. Durations
(`retryAfter`) are ISO 8601, counted from when the response was sent. Every entry
carries `asked`: whether this venue was consulted for this request: a live ask, or a
fresh read of its published book or live desk price within that source's freshness
window. An estimate no venue gave (a model or reference price) is not consulted, and
an `answered` entry is always consulted. How a card's price was obtained is its own
price basis, never this flag.

so it never appears in `complete` or the JSON reply.

RequoteRequest.description:
Asks the venue of an earlier quote again. Only these fields.

Only that quote's venue (every venue of a multi-leg route) is asked, for the same pair, amount and side,
and the answer is one new held quote with `requoteOf`; the original stays orderable until its own expiry.
A venue's indicative card gets its firm quote this way (every such venue, including one whose
firm quote lives 5 s or less and whose card offers Execute within your limit, `next: order`), like naming
the venue in `filters.venues.include`, under the same desk ask limits. Refusals, each by name: 404
`QUOTE_NOT_FOUND` (unknown or another principal's), 410 `QUOTE_EXPIRED` (over 10 minutes past expiry),
400 `CORRIDOR_NOT_OFFERED`, 403 `SOURCE_NOT_OWNED`,
409 `PERSONAL_TARGET_NOT_ALLOWED` (an API key naming a personal wallet), 400 `WALLET_NOT_ON_CHAIN`,
403 `ACCOUNT_NOT_AVAILABLE`, 403 `VENUE_NOT_AVAILABLE_TO_CREDENTIAL`, 409 `REQUOTE_REFUSED` (the venue's
reason in `message`, its token in `details.reason`), 409 `REQUOTE_NEEDS_WALLET`, 504 `REQUOTE_TIMED_OUT`,
429 `QUOTE_RATE_LIMITED` / `VENUE_FIRM_QUOTE_LIMITED` / `BUDGET_EXHAUSTED` with `Retry-After`.

no completion term) carries none. A window whose completion is pending on any other

Active     → Validating | Paused | Disabled
Inactive   → Validating | Disabled
Paused     → Validating | Disabled
Disabled   → ∅ (terminal; only a TetraFi administrator can re-enable it)

api_key.description:
Send the API key in `X-API-Key`.

**Request signing.** A key with signing enabled (`POST /api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/users/me/api-keys/{keyId}/signing`, which returns the signing secret once) must also sign every request:

- `X-Timestamp`: the current Unix time in seconds, within 300 seconds of the server clock.
- `X-Signature`: lower-case hex HMAC-SHA256 of the canonical string, keyed with the signing secret's 32 bytes (the secret is 64 hex characters; decode it first).

The canonical string is four lines joined by `\n`, with no trailing newline: the `X-Timestamp` value, the upper-case method, the path with its query exactly as sent (`/api/v1/orders?limit=1`), and the lower-case hex SHA-256 of the exact body bytes (the SHA-256 of an empty body when there is none).

A write's signature (POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE) is accepted once: sending the same signed write again is refused, so a retry signs again. A read (GET, HEAD) changes nothing, so an identical signed read inside the window is admitted again and polling needs no nonce.

A signing refusal is a 401 `AUTH_REQUIRED` whose `details.reason` names the cause: `SIGNATURE_REQUIRED` (a header is missing), `SIGNATURE_INVALID` (a malformed header or a wrong signature), `TIMESTAMP_OUT_OF_RANGE` or `SIGNATURE_REPLAYED`.

info.description:
TetraFi is an API for institutional trading across on-chain and off-chain venues: discover assets, request quotes, place an order by quote id and read its status. API keys sign every request.

Asset-pair quotes: every tagged union is tagged by `kind`; only the outcome of `/prices` rows and `sources[]` entries is tagged by `status`.

get.summary: List the active workspace's Basic and Advanced orders in newest-first order.

post.description: Place an order by the id of a quote you hold (`{quoteId}` from POST /quotes). A venue (Basic) quote becomes a venue trade (`basicTrade`); a protocol (Advanced) quote becomes a protocol order (`advancedTrade`), after POST /orders/preflight and any wallet signature or source transaction it asks for. Each quote is ordered once: the same quote again answers QUOTE_ALREADY_ORDERED, and a replay with the same Idempotency-Key and body returns the first answer. Read what a quote produced with GET /orders/by-quote/{quoteId}.

parameters.description: Makes a retry safe. Required for API keys (a missing key answers 400 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED); optional for signed-in members. 1 to 255 bytes, unique per order you mean to place; a UUID is a good choice. A retry with the same key and the same body, from the same credential's owner in the same workspace within 24 hours, returns the first answer and never places a second order. The same key with a different body answers 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT; another principal's key answers 403 IDEMPOTENCY_AUTHORITY_REQUIRED. A retry that arrives while the first request is still running waits for it, and answers 409 ORDER_IN_PROGRESS (with Retry-After) if it is still running after 30 seconds. Refusals are not stored: after one, fix the request and send it again with the same key or a new one.
parameters.name: Idempotency-Key

200.description: Order created: a tagged QuoteOrderResponse (`advancedTrade` or `basicTrade`). A Basic trade on an on-chain venue (for example Uniswap v3, paid from an organisation wallet) answers 200 as soon as the order is durable, with `status: working`, before its wallet signs: signing and broadcast run after the answer. Read the order (GET /orders/{orderId}) or subscribe to `order.updated` for its outcome: `settled`, or `unfilled` (terminal) with `operation.dispatch.outcomeCode: not_sent` and `notSentReason: ON_CHAIN_UNSENT` when no swap was sent (an approval may have been mined first, spending its network fee). A refusal before the order exists (limits, compliance, funds, authority) still answers here with its code. A refusal found after the order is claimed but before its wallet is asked (the LP relationship, the venue registry, the audit record or your authority changed) also answers here with its own code, and that order reads `unfilled` with `outcomeCode: not_sent`.

Idempotent-Replayed.description: `true` when this answer was released from the stored receipt of an earlier request with the same Idempotency-Key and body, rather than produced now. Absent on a first answer.

post.description: The asset-pair contract (PairQuoteRequest or RequoteRequest); the legacy intent body is retired, so an object without `sell` or `requote` is 400 INVALID_REQUEST naming `sell`. Validated in order (INVALID_REQUEST naming the field, REQUOTE_FIELDS_CONFLICT, UNKNOWN_ASSET / UNKNOWN_CHAIN / UNKNOWN_VENUE naming the value, ASSET_NOT_ON_CHAIN (a side's Asset has no deployment on the chain pinned for it), INVALID_AMOUNT, SAME_ASSET_NEEDS_CHAIN, CHAIN_PIN_NEEDS_ON_CHAIN, out-of-range INVALID_REQUEST, ROUTING_OPTIONS_FORBIDDEN), then the request_quotes capability, and answered with a PairQuoteSet: every venue planned, venue-hitting plans limited to one every 3 s per principal (429 QUOTE_RATE_LIMITED with Retry-After; cache-only plans are not limited), quotes held for their owner and the set recorded for GET /quotes/requests/{quoteRequestId}. A requote body asks only the earlier quote's venue again (every venue of a multi-leg route, which answers that same route), as JSON (never a stream), and answers a PairQuoteSet whose one quote names it in requoteOf; the earlier quote stays held until its own expiry. Requote refusals: 400 CORRIDOR_NOT_OFFERED / WALLET_NOT_ON_CHAIN (a custody vault or registered workspace address bound to a chain it is not an account of; also on a fresh request), 403 SOURCE_NOT_OWNED / ACCOUNT_NOT_AVAILABLE / VENUE_NOT_AVAILABLE_TO_CREDENTIAL, 404 QUOTE_NOT_FOUND (unknown and another principal's quote alike), 409 REQUOTE_REFUSED (details.reason) / REQUOTE_NEEDS_WALLET / PERSONAL_TARGET_NOT_ALLOWED / QUOTE_CANNOT_BE_REFRESHED (a quote recorded before it could be refreshed for a broker's client), 410 REQUOTE_WINDOW_CLOSED (10 minutes after its expiry, past retainUntil; next search: request quotes again), 429 QUOTE_RATE_LIMITED / VENUE_FIRM_QUOTE_LIMITED /BUDGET_EXHAUSTED with Retry-After, 503 QUOTE_STORE_UNAVAILABLE / QUOTE_NOT_READY, 504 REQUOTE_TIMED_OUT. Every refusal, at every status, is the one error body ApiError {error, message, requestId, timestamp, next?, details?}. Optional filters narrow the auction. Orderable venue-account cards require a current MFA human Company/Broker session, or an API key holding workspace_venue_trade with its venue switch enabled and HMAC request signing. A member key with quotes_request but no venue-trading authority receives native indicative cards (firm false, expiresAt null) with sourceRefusal venueTradeScopeRequired and a re-issuance remedy, without any firm ask. On-chain sources without an organisation wallet grant are indicative with sourceRefusal onchainWalletNotUsable and a wallet-grant remedy; no signer is resolved. Quote-only observations never spend firm-quote budget, and their held refusal is returned if ordered. An API key quotes with quotes_request (which needs orders_write on the same key); it has no Default wallet of a member, so it binds a workspace wallet in bind.wallets: a workspace custody wallet, or an organisation wallet the key was granted (without that grant the source reads API_KEY_ORGANISATION_WALLET_SCOPE_REQUIRED), never a personal one (409 PERSONAL_TARGET_NOT_ALLOWED); its protocol venues remain non-orderable until it binds one; quote-only observations may show a native indicative price without borrowing a wallet. A desk on a production site is firm-asked only on request, the same for sessions and API keys, each one call: name it in filters.venues.include and its firm quote returns in that response, or requote its indicative card ({requote: quoteId}). A broad request never asks it: its card stays indicative and reads unavailable priceOnRequest when it publishes no price. Its next is requote, except where its firm quote lives 5 s or less: then it is order (execute within my limit), and that order makes the one ask, trading only at or above the person's minReceive; a requote of that card (Get firm quote) also asks it once under the same desk limits and returns a firm, executable card with its expiresAt. A sandbox or testnet desk that publishes nothing is firm-asked on a person's or API caller's request within the desk limits (firmQuoteLimited with retryAfter when they are reached); automation principals get it on requote only. On a venue-account card, bind.deliverTo {kind: address, chain, address, destinationTag?} names where the trade's output is withdrawn when the order for it fills: one of the workspace's own wallets that is an approved withdrawal destination of that venue account, for the receipt asset, with exactly that destination tag or memo. The card then carries that deliverTo, a network fee line for the venue's withdrawal fee (the most the order will pay; a higher fee at send refuses) and a receive net of it (netReceived unavailable withdrawalFeeUnread when the fee could not be read), and a requote keeps it. A venue that cannot deliver there answers its source unavailable with DESTINATION_NOT_APPROVED, DELIVER_TO_NOT_A_WORKSPACE_WALLET, WITHDRAWAL_CHAIN_UNSUPPORTED (no withdrawal network for that chain on the site; test sites have none), DELIVER_TO_AMBIGUOUS, WITHDRAWAL_FEE_EXCEEDS_AMOUNT, deliverToCalldataUnsupported or deliverToNotPermitted (deliverTo needs a member session with ViewWallets; an API key lists no deliverTo candidates, and a requote naming one answers 409 REQUOTE_REFUSED with details.reason deliverToNotPermitted). The request spends one Quote token; connection indicative pacing is reported on cards.

sources.detail: This account is still being set up. Complete its required activation steps in Treasury before requesting prices.

200.description: Quotes aggregated successfully: a PairQuoteSet. Accept: text/event-stream selects JSON-data SSE events: quote (PairQuote), source (QuoteSourceEntry), complete (PairQuoteSet), error. A venue the workspace's LP relationship does not allow reads restricted venueRelationship with neutral words in detail and is never asked. Event IDs increase monotonically; the stream includes keepalive comments. Example: broad USD 25000 to USDC, Selini source unavailable accountSetupIncomplete and asked=false; captured live (rfq 2ef31a1ea), one of twelve sources retained and referenceMid omitted. No Selini price or firm ask is implied; Selini USD settlement precision is six decimal places.

get.description: Requires current ViewWallets authority in a Company/Broker workspace (or an admitted LP taker). API keys and OAuth clients additionally require treasury_read; this read never authorizes a payment. Read through the connection holding the account's balance credential, a configured one first (its `connectionId` and execution type are in the body); the observation, staleness and display-value rules are those of the venue-connection balance read, so a balance key held only by a disabled venue returns its last-known balance. 409 VENUE_ACCOUNT_FUNDS_IN_WALLETS for an account whose money is in registered wallets, VENUE_ACCOUNT_REVERIFY_REQUIRED when no current key holds its balance, VENUE_ACCOUNT_REVOKED for a disconnected account, VENUE_ACCOUNT_VENUE_UNKNOWN when its venue is not recognised; 404 VENUE_ACCOUNT_NOT_FOUND. 403 VENUE_READ_AUTHORITY_REFUSED whenever the caller's read authority has ended, whether the check before the read or a recheck during it sees it (reason `authority_ended`: the credential is revoked or expired, or no longer carries treasury_read; reason `permission_withdrawn`: its principal lost ViewWallets, its membership or taker admission); a session that has itself ended answers 401.

get.summary: Read the venue account's balances at its venue

get.description: Requires current ViewWallets authority in a Company/Broker workspace (or an admitted LP taker). API keys and OAuth clients additionally require treasury_read. Read through the configured connection holding the account's balance credential, with the venue-connection deposit-history rules. A bounded window, not a paged list: each answer is one live read of the venue's own credit history for `lookbackDays` (1 to 30, default 7) ending now, returned whole with its `since`, `until`, `observedAt` and `expiresAt`. A window holding more than 1,000 venue records answers no credits, with reasonCode DEPOSIT_HISTORY_WINDOW_TOO_LARGE; read a shorter window. No cursor is offered because the venues' histories have no position that stays stable from one live read to the next, so a cursor could skip or repeat a credit. The 409 refusals of the account balance read, plus VENUE_ACCOUNT_FUNDING_VENUE_DISABLED when only a disabled venue holds the balance key. 403 VENUE_READ_AUTHORITY_REFUSED whenever the caller's read authority has ended, whether the check before the read or a recheck during it sees it (reason `authority_ended`: the credential is revoked or expired, or no longer carries treasury_read; reason `permission_withdrawn`: its principal lost ViewWallets, its membership or taker admission); a session that has itself ended answers 401.

get.summary: Read the venue account's deposit history

get.description: Requires current ViewWallets authority in a Company/Broker workspace (or an admitted LP taker). API keys additionally require treasury_read; this read never authorizes a payment. Read through the configured connection holding the account's balance credential. Select currency for bank instructions: bankDeposit states available, referenceOnly, notOffered or unread, with a reason and reasonCode. Available receiving coordinates or a reference-only result are in bankInstructions. notOffered comes only from the venue's declared bank offering; failed source reads are unread, never notOffered. The answer is Cache-Control no-store and every receiving-account or full-reference disclosure is audited. The connection read's selection and fee rules apply. The account balance read's 409 refusals also apply, plus VENUE_ACCOUNT_FUNDING_VENUE_DISABLED when only a disabled venue holds the balance key. 403 VENUE_READ_AUTHORITY_REFUSED whenever the caller's read authority has ended, whether the check before the read or a recheck during it sees it (reason `authority_ended`: the credential is revoked or expired, or no longer carries treasury_read; reason `permission_withdrawn`: its principal lost ViewWallets, its membership or taker admission); a session that has itself ended answers 401.

parameters.description: ISO fiat currency for the bank-deposit read; never with `asset` or `chainRef`.
parameters.name: currency

parameters.description: The dedicated fiat venue's linked bank id for the sending bank. Required with currency for a dedicated fiat venue and refused for other venues.
parameters.name: providerBankId

bankDeposit.reason: The deposit reference was read from the bound venue account. The venue does not publish its receiving bank details over its API: its own app shows them next to this reference. No deposit has been confirmed.

expectedArrival.source: VALR S20 https://support.valr.com/hc/en-us/articles/360028737292 "How long does it take for my Rand (ZAR) deposit to reflect in my VALR account?" (updated 2026-10-12T13:34:54Z, retrieved 2026-10-15)

capabilities.reason: Independent account evidence is not implemented for this provider.

example.reason: The deposit reference was read from the bound venue account. The venue does not publish its receiving bank details over its API: its own app shows them next to this reference. No deposit has been confirmed.

get.summary: Read how to deposit into the venue account

get.description: A Company/Broker current human session, or an API key or service account with treasury_read whose principal holds ViewWallets. Each venue account with its venue, where its funds are held, its wallets, linked accounts and execution types, each venue's key state, and whether disabling that venue would retire its key. Each item's `accountId` is the `{venueAccountId}` of `GET …/venue-accounts/{venueAccountId}/balances`, `/deposit-history` and `/deposit-instructions`. Oldest first, paged by `limit` (default 20, at most 100) and the opaque `cursor` from the previous page's `nextCursor`; `nextCursor` is null on the last page. 400 INVALID_CURSOR for a cursor this list did not issue. 403 VENUE_READ_AUTHORITY_REFUSED when the caller's authority to read venue accounts has ended (reason `authority_ended`: the credential is revoked or expired, or no longer carries treasury_read; reason `permission_withdrawn`: its principal lost ViewWallets, its membership or taker admission). A session that has itself ended answers 401.

parameters.description: Opaque `nextCursor` from the previous page of the same list and filters.
parameters.name: cursor

post.description: Create a webhook with a shown-once whsec_<base64> secret. Standard Webhooks sends webhook-id, webhook-timestamp (Unix seconds), and webhook-signature: v1,<base64 HMAC-SHA256>, signing id.timestamp.rawBody with the base64-decoded key. Verify the exact raw body and enforce five-minute timestamp tolerance. API keys require webhooks_manage and current manage_webhooks permission. Human sessions require manage_webhooks or manage_credentials.

get.description: The one trade history. Projections: scope=workspace (default) reads the workspace's taker orders and venue trades; a member without view_compliance reads only their own, whatever the scope. scope=mine reads the caller's own (a member session only). scope=umbrella reads a broker's clients' orders with each client category's field visibility (view_umbrella_compliance). perspective=maker reads an LP workspace's fills with pseudonymised counterparties (view_settlements); with settlementStage or minAgeSeconds, its unsettled orders by stage (view_bilateral_documents). The default perspective is taker in every workspace. Every row carries tradeId, kind (order or venueTrade) and projection. Page with limit and cursor; format=csv returns the same filtered rows. Accepts a member session or an API key with trades_read; CSV is a member session only.

parameters.description:
mine, workspace or umbrella. Default: workspace. umbrella needs a broker
workspace and view_umbrella_compliance; mine needs a member session.
parameters.name: scope

parameters.description:
taker (default, in every workspace) or maker. maker needs an LP workspace and
view_settlements.
parameters.name: perspective

parameters.description:
all, order or venueTrade. Default: all for taker and umbrella; for maker the
fills default (on-chain orders); umbrella has orders only.
parameters.name: kind

parameters.description: Settlement status filter, as the projection names it.
parameters.name: status

parameters.description:
Counterparty: the LP's catalogue venue id, the row's `lpVenueId` (taker; a venue
trade matches its execution type's venue), the client workspace (umbrella) or the
taker (maker).
parameters.name: counterpartyId

parameters.description: One of the LP's own venues, by its id (maker only).
parameters.name: venueId

parameters.description:
The member or client who placed the order: member (taker), user id (umbrella),
entity (maker).
parameters.name: client

parameters.description: Settlement stage of an unsettled order (maker only).
parameters.name: settlementStage

parameters.description: Only orders at least this many seconds old (maker only, with settlementStage).
parameters.name: minAgeSeconds

parameters.description: Placed at or after this RFC 3339 instant (umbrella: a UTC midnight).
parameters.name: from

parameters.description: Placed at or before this RFC 3339 instant (umbrella: a UTC midnight).
parameters.name: to

parameters.description: Page size; the projection's own bounds apply (default 25).
parameters.name: limit

parameters.description: The nextCursor of the previous page.
parameters.name: cursor

parameters.description: json (default) or csv. csv returns the projection's export of the same filters.
parameters.name: format

parameters.description: Taker: comma-separated lifecycle buckets (inProgress, completed, failed, refunded, unknown). Maker: the fills lifecycle filter
parameters.name: lifecycle

parameters.description: Taker: taker, support, counterparty or none
parameters.name: nextActor

parameters.description: Taker: either side's display asset symbol (case-insensitive)
parameters.name: asset

parameters.description: Taker: wallet address (custody vault or linked wallet)
parameters.name: address

parameters.description: The row's routingPath type: direct or via_broker
parameters.name: routingPath

parameters.description: Field to sort by, as the projection names it
parameters.name: sortBy

parameters.description: Taker: only orders whose nextAction is present
parameters.name: actionRequired

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds to wait before retrying. Always sent on 429; sent on 503 when the wait is known. `details.retryAfter` carries the same wait as an ISO 8601 duration.

x-ratelimit-limit.description: Sent only when the request's API key has its own requests-per-minute limit: that limit. Sessions, and keys without their own limit, never receive it.

x-ratelimit-remaining.description: Requests left before this caller is limited: the per-address limit's when that limit counted the request, otherwise the API key's own remaining allowance. Absent when no finite limit counted the request.

x-ratelimit-reset.description: Sent with x-ratelimit-limit, only when the request's API key has its own limit: whole seconds until that allowance is full again.
